reviews.title: Super clean case but with one ironic flaw
reviews.comment: So the case is exceptionally well designed and easy to build in, the quality is a lot better compared to MSI cases in the past and the aesthetics are just beautiful. The one flaw is that MSI decided to use 3 pin fans for the 4 provided fans so you won't get pwm controls, if you plan on using different fans then it shouldn't pose as an issue. For me personally it isn't a huge deal breaker as I normally run my applications/games, monitor my temps, adjust my fan speeds to a fixed speed and leave it at that. The fans running at 100% isn't loud surprisingly with great airflow, I have the stock fans running into a splitter with fan reduction set to 60% operation so they're silent and still moving adequate air for my components. Main reason I wanted to use stock fans was to save cost plus the 3 intake fans are reverse blade design so no backside fan support bracket exposed. There are a couple of fans on the market with reverse blade designs that I've used that I prefer not to use again because I'm not a huge fan of the design or software issues.. "cough" thermaltake tt rgb plus. I wanted simple so the stock fans did just fine but better with a splitter that has a resistor in it for reduction in operation. If MSI could in the future go with 4pin PWM fans so speeds can be controlled either bios or software it would definitely be an easy 5 stars but given the fact it's also 2024 to even use 3 pin fans is comical and sad especially when you're trying to market this case with project zero as an innovative leap..

reviews.title: very straightforward case for MSI project zero
reviews.comment: The case is very well built and highly compatible with Project zero and Lian li products.  Case is whisper quiet even under load when playing games at 1440p,  very clean with little to no cables showing upfront.  Just be careful when closing the back panel as whatever clearance you have for cables may push it open.  If MSI were to improve on this design I highly recommend they go for magnetic seals as opposed to plastic clips and prongs, as this was an issue I had with Thermaltake's Tower 300 case.  Also be aware of the ARGB hub on the back, as mine came with one of the screws stripped already from whomever shipped it or checked for distribution.
